decision.title: Incremental bytes: the byte reader and the text window (packet 7.6f)
decision.summary: A streamed document can be read through an sxml_byte_reader in processor.h, and the parser decodes its input into a a part at a time, giving up text already parsed.

body.p: , after , , , , , , . Replaces 's "not bounded yet: the decoded text" for documents read through a byte reader, and 's "bytes delivered incrementally to the parser" (its planned interface, made as planned). perf-3's grammar and token shape () are unchanged.

item.p: Header (processor.h, additive, the rule of for stable headers): sxml_byte_reader (glossary ), whose read operation fills the front of a buffer sxml lends and says whether the input ends there (sxml_byte_reading), the form SXML_RESOURCE_FORM_BYTE_READER of SXML_RESOURCE_KIND_XML_DOCUMENT, and the field sxml_resource.byte_reader, borrowed until release (as for BYTES). A failed read is SXML_STATUS_INPUT_OUTPUT_FAILED: FODC0002 for fn:doc and for a streamed document. Only a streamed document (xsl:source-document streamable="yes", a streamed principal source, , ) is parsed as its bytes arrive; fn:doc and the other uses read the reader whole first (its tree holds the document anyway). Other kinds keep BYTES (a reader there is a form the kind does not allow). Rejected: a reader in sxml_xml_parse_request (xml.h, a second way to give input to every parse; the incremental parse request, internal, takes it instead), and a pull of the next bytes into memory the reader owns (the parser would copy anyway, and the lent buffer keeps the reader free of allocation).

The text window (new src/xml_input.c, glossary ): the part of a document's decoded UTF-8 text the parser holds. The input, given whole or through a reader, is decoded a part at a time (at least 32 KB, and at least as much again as the window holds, so scans that find no cut stay linear) as the head and the content segments need it (); before a segment is cut, the text before it is given up when as much goes as stays. A part ends at a character boundary of the input: a UTF-8 sequence or a UTF-16 unit or surrogate pair not complete waits for the next read (XML 1.0, 4.3.3; RFC 2781), and in XML 1.1 a last CR waits for the character after it (CR NEL is one line end, a CR before LINE SEPARATOR stays one, 2.11). Each part is checked as the whole text was: U+0000 ([2] Char), the restricted characters of XML 1.1 ([2a]); NEL and LINE SEPARATOR translated. The encoding is detected from the first bytes, read up to the first '>' (Appendix F), and the XML declaration's version from the first part. A whole input in UTF-8 or US-ASCII without XML 1.1 line ends to translate stays its own text, checked at once and not copied, as before; UTF-16 and ISO-8859-1 input given whole is now decoded a window at a time too ( kept a whole UTF-8 copy). The position tracker reads the window and keeps a floor (the start of the text it still holds, with its line and column), and the names of the open elements, which the start tags before a segment repeat, are copied rather than viewed.

Behaviour: a decoding error of a UTF-16 or ISO-8859-1 input, or of any input read through a reader, is found when its part is decoded, so the events of the content before it come first (as made it for syntax errors); its location is the same. Documents stay below 4 GB ().

CLI: the file reader (apps/cli_framework/cli_command.h) has two optional operations, open_file and close_file, a file read a part at a time through a byte reader (the platform's over ISO C stdio); the resolver of the query and transform commands delivers XML documents that way (standard input stays read whole). No command or flag changes.
JavaScript: the host keeps delivering BYTES (the table resolver); nothing changes there.

Measured (release, sxml transform, a generated 95.6 MB document of 904,745 records, peak resident set, outputs byte-identical): the streamed identity (on-no-match shallow-copy) 133.9 MB before, 11.0 MB after (29 s either way); a for-each over the hot records under "/" 134.5 MB to 11.0 MB; the same document in UTF-16 (191 MB) 11.0 MB; a 974 MB document 10.9 MB for the for-each (103 s), so the gate's "1 GB under 64 MB" holds for the process (the identity of 974 MB stops at the CLI's default evaluation step limit, at 11.0 MB). Unit tests (tests/xml_test.c): every way of reading (whole, incremental, through a reader giving 1 to 97 bytes at a time) gives the same events, locations and failure positions in UTF-8 with and without a byte order mark, UTF-16 LE and BE, ISO-8859-1 and XML 1.1 with NEL, CR NEL and LINE SEPARATOR; 3.9 MB (UTF-16) and 2 MB read through a reader take 273 KB and 141 KB of parser memory (test limit 512 KB). XT40 and QT4 XQ40 (release, whole suites, case by case): no outcome changes (XT40 11,918 passed, XQ40 45,914); xmlconf unchanged.

Not done (packet 7.6f's other items): xsl:merge with streamed inputs and capture="yes" end rules while streaming, below and in the task file; both need new IR (a MERGE form, a capture function among sxml_ir_stream_accumulators) and a new evaluator part, in src/ir_internal.h, src/ir.c, src/ir_verify.c, src/evaluator.c and src/evaluator_machine_internal.h, which packet 4.21 holds uncommitted.

xsl:merge with streamed inputs (15.3, 15.4, 18.2): a part MERGE over one cursor per anchor document of each streamable merge source: an open streamed document () and the source's select, a striding downward path, advanced to its next selected node, which is grounded in a full window; the cursor keeps that item and its merge keys (computed by the source's key functions in the item's focus). Each step takes the smallest current key in merge-key order (the comparison of the sort, source order breaking ties), gathers the current items of every cursor equal to it, binds the group as the grounded merge does (current-merge-group, -key, the source names), runs the merge-action and advances the cursors it took. XTDE2220 when a cursor's next key is smaller than its last. Memory: the depth of each document and one window per cursor.

capture="yes" (19.9): a fifth function capture-K($node) that says at an element's start whether an end rule with capture="yes" matches it; the stream builder then tees the element's events into a full window, nested captures on a stack, and end-K reads that window instead of the shallow one. Memory: the captured subtrees.
